userStories.title: Discover user skills from ~/.agents/skills
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add an agents-user skills package to the shared resource catalog with explicit first-wins precedence.

**Motivation** — Skills a user installed under `~/.agents/skills/` (13 on the reporting machine) never reach the chat catalog.

**Approach** — **US-002 — `~/.agents/skills`.** A path helper next to `naxAgentsDir`:

```ts
// packages/nax/src/resources/claude-paths.ts
/** The user-level skills directory other coding agents read: `<home>/.agents/skills`. */
export function agentsSkillsDir(): string; // join(_claudePathsDeps.homedir(), ".agents", "skills")
```

`ResourceOrigin` gains `{ readonly kind: "agents-user" }`, and `originLabel` returns `"agents-user"` for it. `loadResourceCatalog` builds an `agents-user` package beside `naxUserPackage`: `scanSkillsDir(agentsSkillsDir(), { kind: "agents-user" })`, id `"agents-user"`, `root` = that directory, skills only (no commands, agents, MCP servers or hooks). An absent directory yields no package and no diagnostic, as `naxUserPackage` does. The package loads whatever `config.resources.claudeCode` says. Package order: `claude-project`, `nax-user`, `agents-user`, then `claude-user` and Claude plugins, then nax plugin packages; with no repo package, `nax-user` then `agents-user` come first. `withNaxUser` (`catalog.ts`) takes the list of user packages to insert (`nax-user`, `agents-user`, each optional) instead of one, so the insertion point rule is unchanged. `loadResourceCatalog` is shared, so every catalog consumer sees `agents-user` skills by design: `nax chat`, `nax agents run`, the `nax run` skills provider (`runtime/index.ts`) and `nax mcp`. `buildResourceCatalog` keeps first-wins name resolution, so a repo skill wins a name clash with an `agents-user` skill, which wins over a `~/.claude/skills` or plugin skill.

Because `agentsSkillsDir()` reads the real home directory, catalog tests that call `loadResourceCatalog` set `_claudePathsDeps.homedir` to a temporary directory (see `### Modifies`).

### Modifies
- `packages/nax/test/unit/resources/nax-user-agents.test.ts` — `load()` reads the real home directory for the user skills directory, so the test "packages order nax-user after claude-project and before claude-user" would list an `agents-user` package on a machine that has one; the file sets `_claudePathsDeps.homedir` to its temporary directory in `beforeEach` and restores it in `afterEach`, and that expected order stays `["claude-project", "nax-user", "claude-user", "p@m"]`.
- `packages/nax/test/unit/resources/catalog.test.ts` — any `loadResourceCatalog` call would pick up a real user skills directory (its package-list assertions are closed-world); the file sets `_claudePathsDeps.homedir` to a temporary directory in `beforeEach` and restores it in `afterEach`, with every existing expectation unchanged.
- `packages/nax/test/unit/resources/claude-sources.test.ts` — any `loadResourceCatalog` call would pick up a real user skills directory; the file sets `_claudePathsDeps.homedir` to a temporary directory in `beforeEach` and restores it in `afterEach`, with every existing expectation unchanged.
- `packages/nax/test/unit/cli/mcp-lock.test.ts` — its `loadResourceCatalog` calls would read a real user skills directory; the file sets `_claudePathsDeps.homedir` to a temporary directory in `beforeEach` and restores it in `afterEach`, with every existing expectation unchanged.
- `packages/nax/test/unit/cli/chat-resources.test.ts` — its `loadResourceCatalog` calls would read a real user skills directory; the file sets `_claudePathsDeps.homedir` to a temporary directory in `beforeEach` and restores it in `afterEach`, with every existing expectation unchanged.

**Scope** — In: path helper, ResourceOrigin/label, optional skills-only user package, ordering and hermetic discovery fixtures. Out: forge overrides (US-001), abort reasons (US-003/US-004), task registry/provider/lifecycle changes (US-005/US-006/US-007). A repo-level `.agents/skills/` directory is not loaded; only the user-level `~/.agents/skills/`. Skills under `~/.agents/skills` are not given an env-var override for their location.

**Interface** —
```ts
export function agentsSkillsDir(): string;
```
`ResourceOrigin` gains `{ readonly kind: "agents-user" }`.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] agentsSkillsDir() with _claudePathsDeps.homedir returning /home/u returns /home/u/.agents/skills.
[unit] originLabel({ kind: "agents-user" }) returns "agents-user".
[unit] loadResourceCatalog with _claudePathsDeps.homedir pointing at a temporary home holding .agents/skills/foo/SKILL.md returns a catalog whose findSkill("foo") has origin kind "agents-user".
[unit] loadResourceCatalog with that home and config.resources.claudeCode false still finds skill foo.
[unit] With no .agents/skills directory in the temporary home, the catalog's package ids do not contain "agents-user".
[unit] With no .agents/skills directory, the catalog's diagnostics hold no entry whose path is under the temporary home's .agents directory.
[unit] With a repo skill at <repoRoot>/.claude/skills/foo/SKILL.md and an agents-user skill foo, findSkill("foo") has origin kind "claude-project".
[unit] With an agents-user skill foo and a Claude user skill at <CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR>/skills/foo/SKILL.md, findSkill("foo") has origin kind "agents-user".

[unit] With a repo package, a nax-user agent, an agents-user skill, a Claude user settings file and one enabled Claude plugin p@m, the catalog's package ids are ["claude-project", "nax-user", "agents-user", "claude-user", "p@m"].

userStories.title: Name ACP abandoned-tool reasons
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Carry explicit ACP-owned turn-end reasons into abandoned embedder tool results without changing caller-owned cancel reasons.

**Motivation** — The ACP client's `abandoned(name)` names none, so those turn ends still read only `the turn ended.`.

**Approach** — **US-004 — ACP abandoned reason.** In `packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/tool-calls.ts`, `abandoned(name)` becomes `abandoned(name, signal)`, with the same rule as US-003. The ACP package keeps its own copies, because neither `abandonedToolMessage` nor `TurnEndAbort` is exported from `@nathapp/nax-agent`'s public entry: a new `packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/turn-end-abort.ts` exports `class TurnEndAbort extends Error { override readonly name = "AbortError" }` and `abandonedText(name: string, signal: AbortSignal): string` (`NaxError` reason gives `(<code>: <message>)`, a `TurnEndAbort` reason gives `(<message>)`, anything else the bare text). Both callers pass the signal they raced (`ctx.signal` in `invoke`, `signal` in `run`). The reasonless sources get `TurnEndAbort` reasons:

- `client/tool-host.ts`: `gone.abort(new TurnEndAbort("the agent closed the tool request"))` when the HTTP response closes, and `state.stopped.abort(new TurnEndAbort("the tool host stopped"))` in `stop()`;
- `client/inbound.ts`: the binding's `scope.abort()` on detach becomes `scope.abort(new TurnEndAbort("the ACP prompt turn ended"))`;
- `client/backend.ts`: `gone.abort()` when the agent process exits becomes `gone.abort(new TurnEndAbort("the agent process exited"))`.

A caller's own cancel or timeout signal keeps whatever reason it carried; a `NaxError` reason is named as today. Existing ACP tests that abort with no argument and assert the bare text (`tool-calls.test.ts`, `backend-tools.test.ts`) stay green unchanged.

For the HTTP-response-close integration criterion, observe the accepted server-side ToolCalls.call promise and its error text; a disconnected HTTP client cannot receive a reply over the closed socket. Use the existing fake ACP launch seam for the process-exit criterion.

The exact abandoned text rule is: a NaxError yields `Tool "<name>" was abandoned: the turn ended (<code>: <message>).`; this package's TurnEndAbort yields `Tool "<name>" was abandoned: the turn ended (<message>).`; anything else, including a bare abort's DOMException, yields `Tool "<name>" was abandoned: the turn ended.`.

**Scope** — In: local reason class/formatter, both tool-call abandonment paths and tool-host/inbound/process-exit abort sources. Out: native adapter changes (US-003), background subagent support (US-005/US-006/US-007), forge/skills (US-001/US-002). Do not import nax-agent internals or expose a new public API; preserve tool-host authorization and approval policy.

**Interface** —
```ts
export class TurnEndAbort extends Error { override readonly name = "AbortError" }
export function abandonedText(name: string, signal: AbortSignal): string;
```
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] abandonedText("acme__put", signal) for a signal aborted with new TurnEndAbort("the ACP prompt turn ended") returns Tool "acme__put" was abandoned: the turn ended (the ACP prompt turn ended).
[unit] abandonedText("acme__put", signal) for a signal aborted with no argument returns Tool "acme__put" was abandoned: the turn ended.

[unit] abandonedText("acme__put", signal) for a signal aborted with new NaxError("cancelled", "AGENT_SESSION_CANCELLED") returns Tool "acme__put" was abandoned: the turn ended (AGENT_SESSION_CANCELLED: cancelled).

[unit] A tool call through the ACP client's tool-call runner whose signal is aborted with new TurnEndAbort("the tool host stopped") while the tool runs returns an error result with text Tool "<name>" was abandoned: the turn ended (the tool host stopped).

[unit] A tool call whose signal is already aborted with new TurnEndAbort("the tool host stopped") before it starts returns an error result with text `Tool "<name>" was abandoned: the turn ended (the tool host stopped).` (the same text as the in-flight abort path).

[unit] Detaching an inbound binding (calling the function createInboundRouter(...).attach(...) returned) while one of its tool calls runs answers that call with text ending (the ACP prompt turn ended).
[integration] Stopping the tool host while a tool call it accepted is running answers that call with text ending (the tool host stopped).
[integration] Closing the HTTP response of a tool-host request while its tool call runs answers that call with text ending (the agent closed the tool request).
[unit] When the ACP agent process exits while a tool call bound to its session runs, the call is answered with text ending (the agent process exited).

routing.reasoning: Existing signal fan-in and abandonment races remain in place; this adds a local formatter and reason arguments at four abort sites. Session lifecycle paths still require strict isolated TDD.

suggestedCriteria: abandonedText returns the bare abandoned text for a signal aborted with new DOMException("other", "AbortError").

userStories.title: Represent background agents in tasks, notices and footer
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] adoptAgent({ agent: "code-reviewer", task: "Review the spec\nat a.md", ended, stop }) returns a sink whose id matches ^agent-[0-9a-f]{8}$.
[unit] After that adoption, list() holds one record with kind: "agent", state: "running", origin: "agent" and command: "code-reviewer: Review the spec".
[unit] A task whose first line is 120 characters long is recorded with a command whose task part is its first 80 characters.

[unit] When ended resolves { outcome: "succeeded", text: "No findings." }, the record's state becomes "succeeded", it has no exitCode, and output(id) contains No findings. and [nax] agent ended: succeeded.

[unit] When ended resolves { outcome: "failed", text: "boom" }, the record's state becomes "failed" and peekNotice() returns text containing [nax-tasks] background agent <id> (code-reviewer: Review the spec) ended: failed, log <logPath>.
[unit] stop(id) on a running agent task calls the handle's stop once and the record's state is "stopped".
[unit] A stopped agent task whose ended later resolves { outcome: "succeeded", text: "late" } stays "stopped" and peekNotice() returns undefined.
[unit] stopAll() with one running shell and one running agent task calls both handles' stop and resolves after both ended promises settle.
[unit] sink.appendLine("[tool] Read") on a running agent task makes output(id) contain [tool] Read.
[unit] sink.appendLine after the task ended adds nothing to output(id).
[unit] running() with one running shell and one running agent task returns both records, the agent one with kind: "agent".
[unit] The nax-tasks provider's stop tool with input { task: "<agent id>" } stops the agent task (its handle's stop is called).
[unit] The nax-tasks provider's output tool with input { task: "<agent id>" } of a known agent task returns its log text.

[unit] buildBackgroundTaskNotice with one ended shell task and one ended agent task returns the shell line unchanged ([nax-tasks] background command <id> (<command>) ended: <state>, exit code <n>, log <path>), then the agent line, then the follow-up line.
[unit] buildBackgroundTasksInstructions() returns text containing nax-agents__run, runInBackground and keeps running after your turn ends.
[unit] summarizeBackgroundNotice of a notice holding one agent line with state succeeded returns 1 background agent ended · 1 succeeded.
[unit] summarizeBackgroundNotice of a notice whose first line is an agent line and second line a shell line, both failed, returns 2 background tasks ended · 2 failed.
[unit] summarizeBackgroundNotice of a notice whose first line is a shell line succeeded and second an agent line failed returns 2 background tasks ended · 1 succeeded · 1 failed.
[unit] summarizeBackgroundNotice of a notice holding only shell lines returns today's text (one succeeded shell: 1 background command ended · 1 succeeded).
[unit] formatJobStrip([], [{ command: "bun test" }, { command: "a: b", kind: "agent" }]) returns 1 shell, the strip's separator, then 1 agent.
[unit] formatJobStrip([], [{ command: "a: b", kind: "agent" }, { command: "c: d", kind: "agent" }]) returns 2 agents.
[unit] formatJobStrip([], [{ command: "bun test" }, { command: "ls" }]) returns 2 shells (today's result).

routing.reasoning: Generalizes a concurrent registry across two handle kinds with log/stop/completion races and propagates kind through notices and UI; session execution is delegated to US-007.

output(id) of a newly adopted agent contains [nax] agent code-reviewer: Review the spec for task Review the spec\nat a.md.

routing.reasoning: Local additive schema/validation/callback dispatch with exact-text and argument-shape compatibility; no session lifecycle or permission implementation changes.

routing.reasoning: Introduces detached concurrent session lifecycles, pending-approval ownership, stop/open/close races and event/cost routing across host and registry; sessions and access-control asks require strict isolated TDD.

suggestedCriteria: When a background session emits a question between parent turns, the chat ask controller receives it and sessionFor(requestId) returns the nested session.
When ChatHost.close() is called while a background session is still opening, the run's opening signal is aborted and no running background task remains after chat close.
After a background run emits turn_end with costUsd 0.25, takeCost() returns 0.25 once and then returns 0.
When a background task is stopped twice through its adopted handle, its nested session is cancelled at most once.

analysis:
Refinement audit: checked the on-disk spec.md against every story. All 104 numbered spec criteria are retained in their original stories and order: US-001 AC1-22, US-002 AC1-12, US-003 AC1-9, US-004 AC1-9, US-005 AC1-22, US-006 AC1-9 and US-007 AC1-21. Restored configuredForgeKind rejection (US-001 AC22), the hanging-model qualifiers on US-003 AC8/9, and ACP HTTP-response-close/process-exit results (US-004 AC8/9); qualified inbound detach as createInboundRouter(...).attach(...). The additional US-007 AC22-24 make the failure table's idle approval, timeout and thrown-error log cases observable, without changing the 21 numbered spec criteria. Every story has a negative path and regression anchor; all 15 feature exclusions remain verbatim. All binding ids, workdirs and dependencies remain unchanged; every spec-recommended context file is included within each five-file limit. Auto-PR must validate optional unknown config through configuredForgeKind/autoPrForge, forge must not acquire a schema default, and the existing registry allocator must accept bash/agent prefixes. ACP remains medium complexity because the existing signal races are reused; strict session-path TDD remains mandatory. HTTP disconnect assertions observe the server-side tool result, and an opening background session is stopped by ChatHost.close/task cleanup rather than assuming closeAll alone aborts unopened sessions.

Existing-code enhancement across three packages, closing #2957, #2959 and #2930; no nax-ai changes or release/version changes are needed. Navigation used direct reads and targeted searches because codebase-memory MCP is unavailable in this host. The seven binding stories are preserved: US-001 through US-006 are independent, and US-007 depends exactly on US-005 and US-006. All paths below are repo-root relative.

Architecture and implementation conventions: docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:19 links the dependency-injection/error-handling conventions, :30 links async/testing/logging patterns and :41 links permission/session conventions. nax is Bun-native; nax-agent and nax-agent-acp must ship Node-compatible ESM with no Bun source APIs. nax-agent uses #src imports or explicit .ts relative imports; ACP may consume nax-agent only through its public root, never /internal. Keep TurnEndAbort private to each package and do not change either public API snapshot. Use mutable _deps seams, restore every override in afterEach, and use existing shared fixtures rather than global monkey-patching or real paid agents. US-003, US-004 and US-007 touch session lifecycles/approval paths and therefore use strict three-session-tdd. Tests belong under test/ mirroring source; nax-agent regression tests must be demonstrated red against the baseline. Run package-scoped targeted Bun tests with explicit paths and timeouts, never bare bun test; automatic pipeline gates handle lint/typecheck/build. Coverage is separate and must not be run inside NAX_SANDBOXED=1.

US-001 findings: packages/nax/src/forge/detect.ts:14 parses hosts; :25 classifies GitHub/GitLab; :37 probes both CLIs and only selects exactly one installed CLI; :54 currently reads origin first. packages/nax/src/forge/types.ts:21 defines ForgeDeps with optional identity(), providing the backward-compatible optional-dependency precedent. packages/nax/src/forge/deps.ts:140 owns defaultForgeDeps; retain its existing hardened git execution and identity/token behavior. packages/nax/src/forge/identity.ts:54 has the process-local mutable capture holder and :78 demonstrates NaxError with stage forge. packages/nax/bin/nax.ts:100 imports the forge barrel and :135 captures identity inside the startup refusal block. Add kind capture to that same block, before command dispatch, including --version. packages/nax/src/forge/index.ts:31-32 exports detection/deps; add the specified kind exports there. packages/nax/src/config/schemas.ts:91 defines NaxConfigSchema and :472 contains the resources block; packages/nax/src/config/runtime-types.ts:339 defines NaxConfig. Add schemas-forge.ts/runtime-types-forge.ts and wire optional forge into both schema and runtime types without a new root-only restriction. packages/nax/src/config/loader.ts:247 loads defaults/global/project/profile/CLI layers, :260 resolves profile chains, :279-286 applies layers. Dynamic import of @/config prevents a static forge-config cycle; resolution catches loading failures and does not cache repo config globally. Env kind is captured once, while config is resolved per repoRoot; command-line --profile overrides are intentionally unavailable to detectForge. Production wiring is already centralized: packages/nax/src/cli/workflow-forge.ts:41, workflow/ci-failures.ts:21, workflow/feature-deps.ts:8-9, bot/review-deps.ts:59 and bot/pr-head-wait.ts:10 use defaultForgeDeps. forge/pr-read.ts:24, cli/workflow-promote.ts:126, cli/workflow-record.ts:114 and workflow/finalize.ts:95 consume detection directly or indirectly. Optional explicitKind keeps legacy fakes unchanged; a defined override must short-circuit before any subprocess. packages/nax/src/plugins/builtin/auto-pr/index.ts:130 defines _autoPrDeps, :222-225 reads remote/classifies in shouldRun, and :261-265 does so in execute. Preserve publishable-branch guards, required origin lookup, push-before-open and post-push duplicate checks; only change forge selection to captured env, validated resolved run config, then remote classification, with no second config load. PostRunContext.config is optional unknown (packages/nax/src/plugins/extensions.ts:259), so do not access context.config.forge directly: add configuredForgeKind(context) with runtime checks and share autoPrForge(context, remoteUrl) between shouldRun and execute. Keep ForgeConfigSchema.optional() without prefault/default; packages/nax/src/config/defaults.ts:11 derives DEFAULT_CONFIG from schema parsing, so absent forge must remain absent. Regression anchors include test/unit/forge/detect.test.ts, identity.test.ts, deps-identity.test.ts and existing auto-PR tests; add the specified capture/resolution/detection/auto-PR tests and CLI subprocess checks. Real-config integration must isolate NAX_GLOBAL_CONFIG_DIR and reset _forgeKind and _forgeKindDeps; otherwise ambient config can alter detection results.

US-002 findings: packages/nax/src/resources/claude-paths.ts:4 supplies the injectable homedir seam and :22 implements naxAgentsDir. packages/nax/src/resources/catalog.ts:15-38 implements first-wins lookup including qualified names, :65 builds nax-user, :87 inserts after a leading claude-project package and :97-112 composes the catalog. Generalize the insertion helper to an ordered list of optional user packages and scan agents-user independently of resources.claudeCode. packages/nax/src/resources/scan-dirs.ts:45-56 already suppresses ENOENT diagnostics and :80 uses */SKILL.md, so reuse that parser/scanner for missing/malformed/one-level behavior. ResourceOrigin is in resources/types.ts:1 and originLabel's exhaustive switch is in resources/listing.ts:6; add agents-user consistently. Shared consumers include cli/chat.ts:263, cli/agents-run.ts:157, runtime/index.ts:347, cli/mcp.ts:58 and execution/lifecycle/run-setup.ts:107; this is intentionally a catalog-wide change, not chat-only. test/unit/resources/nax-user-agents.test.ts:24-40 currently passes isolated Claude/nax roots but does not override homedir, so adding the new source would leak real user skills into closed-world assertions. Also isolate and restore homedir in catalog.test.ts, claude-sources.test.ts, cli/mcp-lock.test.ts and cli/chat-resources.test.ts. Existing expectations remain unchanged; new discovery tests explicitly populate the temporary home. First-wins ordering is the migration behavior: repo, nax-user, agents-user, Claude user/plugins, nax plugins; no resource migration or recursive scan.

US-003 findings: packages/nax-agent/src/native/session-adapter.ts:189 starts sendTurn, :214 resolves timeoutSeconds, :249 registers the reasonless active-call cancel and :265-268 arms the reasonless whole-turn deadline. :325 contains a separate per-round-trip abort which must remain untouched. packages/nax-agent/src/session/session-interaction.ts:150 implements abandonedToolMessage with NaxError-only formatting, :181-187 races embedder work, and the coding-tool/cancel-grace paths share that message helper. Introduce an Error subclass with name AbortError so only nax-owned tagged reasons gain text; do not match arbitrary AbortError/DOMException messages. packages/nax-agent/src/native/session/turn-loop-round-trip.ts:340 rethrows signal.reason verbatim; packages/nax/src/session/manager.ts:598 and session/watchdog-turn-classification.ts:52 recognize Error.name === AbortError. This compatibility requirement rules out plain NaxError reasons at these two native abort sites. Existing regression tests test/unit/session/session-interaction-abandoned.test.ts:72-119 assert NaxError, bare abort and plain Error behavior; session-interaction-cancel-grace.test.ts and native-backend-providers.test.ts must remain green unchanged. Adapter tests should capture _adapterDeps timers and invoke only the first/whole-turn timer, avoiding wall-clock sleeps and accidental round-trip abort races.

US-004 findings: packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/tool-calls.ts:107 currently returns a bare abandoned result, :125-139 races an active tool and :171 has the already-aborted path; both must receive the exact signal being raced. The composite is constructed at :191 from the binding and request signals; preserve first-abort reason semantics rather than overwriting caller reasons. client/inbound.ts:167-181 creates a per-turn scope, combines it with the caller signal and aborts it on detach. client/tool-host.ts:153-168 combines response-close/host-stop signals; :258 aborts stopped. client/backend.ts:212-224 owns the process-exit controller. Add the four precise TurnEndAbort messages without changing HTTP authorization, approval policy, concurrency caps, detach draining or tool result shape. The public nax-agent NaxError may be used for instanceof recognition, but TurnEndAbort and abandonedToolMessage are not public and must not be imported across the boundary. Existing client/tool-calls.test.ts:14-26 imports shared ask fixtures/constants and backend-tools.test.ts anchors bare abort behavior. Add reason tests including already-aborted, inbound detach and real loopback tool-host stop; use the fake launch seam/in-memory agent, never a real external adapter. Network stop/response-close ordering is a race risk: stop must abort accepted work with the host-stop reason before connection teardown causes a competing response-close reason.

US-005 findings: packages/nax/src/chat/background/task-types.ts:6 defines immutable task snapshots and :19 currently accepts bash ids only; ChatBackgroundTasks at :27 extends the existing shell port. task-registry.ts:59 assumes BackgroundCommandHandle; :88-96 owns entries/completions/unnoticed snapshot state; :148 stop marks stopped before calling the handle; :158-162 drains completions; :165-170 allocates collision-checked bash ids; :173 adopts a shell; :209-238 serializes/caps log writes; :240-257 finalizes and queues notices; :268-274 awaits pending log writes for output. Extend handle/entry storage for agents while preserving bounded logs, warning behavior, copied snapshots, notice markSeen and shutdown drain behavior. Agent records have kind agent and no exitCode; shell records keep absent kind and all current fields. Stopped wins a late completion, appendLine after end is ignored and stopped tasks never enqueue notices. tasks-provider.ts:16 validates TASK_ID_PATTERN, :24-26 stops only known running tasks and :40 returns a bounded log; broadening the common id pattern exposes agents automatically without rewriting tool descriptions. prompts/builders/background-builder.ts:4 and :14 own instructions and canonical notices; notice-summary.ts:17 defines the task-line pattern, :26-42 counts states and :51-59 classifies by the first line. Adding a regex capture for kind shifts state to group 2; preserve first-line classification and state insertion order as well as all-shell wording. tui/chat/chat-status.ts:301 defines FooterTask and :314 formats the compact strip: keep workflow-job elision, then shell count, then agent count, omitting zero parts. useJobs already forwards running task records and idle notices; no new notice mechanism or transcript tool stream is needed. Existing task-registry.test.ts, task-registry-notices.test.ts and tasks-provider.test.ts cover shell regression behavior; new tests cover agent lifecycle/logging/notices and mixed footer/summary cases. UI literal fakes named in the spec need no adoptAgent addition because their exercised paths do not call it and test/ is excluded from nax's package typecheck.

US-006 findings: packages/nax/src/chat/agents-provider.ts:9 builds RUN_DESCRIPTION ending in EXPLORE_SENTENCE, :14 defines the existing options, :50 validates task/name/model and :66-95 exposes/dispatches the single run tool. Add optional callback and boolean schema without changing required task/additionalProperties, built-in general fallback, named lookup, unknown-agent result or foreground argument arity. Resolve current input/unknown-agent failures before new background validation; pass no parent signal to the background callback. Named no-model foreground calls currently omit the fourth argument, while general foreground calls pass target.model; preserve these precise baseline call shapes. test/unit/chat/agents-provider.test.ts:15-16 freezes error/explore text and the later description assertions freeze the full run description; update the frozen description copy in the same story, leaving endsWith(EXPLORE_SENTENCE) and required task assertions intact. Provider-only tests stub callbacks; lifecycle belongs in US-007.

US-007 findings: packages/nax/src/chat/subagent-runs.ts:33/52 define deps/public runs, :110-114 separate owner/active/inFlight state, :126-144 releases pending asks, :146-156 attributes/routes asks and :159-174 records usage/spend and optionally forwards tools. :177-188 links foreground runs to parent signals, :190-242 runs nested sessions with common model/tools/memory/session wiring and :259-273 cancels/settles only inFlight and closes active sessions. Add a separate background run set and unlinked controller; share nested wiring without accidentally capturing deps.turnListener for background work. Validate model before adoption, retain foreground model refusal text, and guarantee adopted ended always resolves for success/error/throw/stop. Stop-before-open aborts the opening signal; stop-after-open cancels exactly once. packages/nax/src/chat/subagent-session.ts:30-58 defines input session/signal/event callbacks, :112-114 passes openSignal and approvalTimeoutMs, :145-187 drives/closes sessions and links cancellation. Preserve permissions/profiles/tool narrowing and no nested background registry; avoid double session.cancel when combining controller abort with the existing runOnSession listener. Adoption/log-sink setup must not lose early tool events, including a synchronous fake callback; append only tool_call names, not foreground transcript events. Usage remains source subagent and spend remains deferred to the next cost row. packages/nax/src/chat/chat-host.ts:197 constructs runs before assigning this.tasks at :211-212, so the specified backgroundTasks getter is essential; :216 currently provides only run to createAgentsProvider. :495 and :511 settle nested runs around sends, :557 cancelAll on Esc and :582 closes runs before final host cleanup. Background runs must be unreachable from send settlement/Esc yet remain reachable from task stop/stopAll and chat teardown, including when a session is still opening. Pending approvals/questions must route when idle, remain answerable through sessionFor and release as cancelled on task stop or close. Existing test/unit/chat/subagent-runs.test.ts:1-24 exposes scripted sessions/events/waitForCondition/withDepsRestore helpers, and :34-45 supplies deps fixtures. New background tests must use deterministic deferred work and ensure held runs are released on cleanup; host integration must exercise the provider the host actually built, not a standalone provider fake.

Migration/backward compatibility: all new config/input/origin/kind fields are additive, no stored chat/task format migration is needed, and task logs remain machine-local rather than resumable jobs. Env capture is the only new startup refusal. No override keeps forge behavior unchanged; missing ~/.agents/skills stays silent; foreground subagent lifecycle and bare-abort text stay unchanged. A required adoptAgent method affects concrete ChatBackgroundTasks implementations; audit structural fakes but do not alter the explicitly exempt UI fakes unnecessarily. Main risks are ambient environment/home pollution, config import cycles, losing abort reason identity across AbortSignal.any, mixed regex capture indexing, stop/completion races, late session opens during close, orphaned approvals and event routing into a subsequent parent turn. Keep implementation chunks inside each binding package and consume US-005/US-006 interfaces only after those dependencies have completed.
outOfScope: `NAX_FORGE_KIND` does not change forge identity, tokens or which CLI login is used; it only names the forge kind.
A per-remote or per-host forge map (several forges in one config) is not added; `forge.kind` names one forge for the whole project config.
A repo-level `.agents/skills/` directory is not loaded; only the user-level `~/.agents/skills/`.
Skills under `~/.agents/skills` are not given an env-var override for their location.
A background subagent's spend is added to the chat's nested spend and is reported on the next turn's cost row, not on the turn that started it.
A background subagent's tool calls are not shown in the transcript; they are written to its task log.
A subagent cannot itself start background subagents or background shell commands (nested sessions get no background registry, as today).
A foreground `nax-agents__run` keeps today's lifecycle: it is cancelled when its parent turn ends or is stopped.
Background subagents do not survive closing the chat; close stops them with the other background tasks.
The idle watchdog's and turn deadline's thresholds are not changed; only their abort reasons.
No cap on the number of concurrent background subagents is added; each one is listed in the footer and can be stopped.
The `nax-tasks__list` / `output` / `stop` tool descriptions and the close-confirm wording ("background command(s)") are not reworded for agents.
The native adapter's per-round-trip timer (one complete or summarize call) keeps aborting with no reason.
`forge.kind` set only through a command-line `--profile` is not seen by `detectForge`; it reads the config `loadConfig(repoRoot)` resolves.
`forge.kind` is not pinned as a root-only key; a per-package config may set it like any other key.
